evidence: backend/servers/api-server/src/services/push_fanout.rs:1650 `async fn deliver_job(&self, payload: &str)` — the Redis push_fanout_queue worker. A job is popped off the list via BLPOP (process_pending_jobs :1601, queue_pop_blocking on PUSH_FANOUT_QUEUE_KEY :1486, up to MAX_JOBS_PER_TICK=256 :1498 per tick). On a GENUINE transient failure the job is logged and DROPPED with no re-queue, no backoff, and no dead-letter: the `Err(e) =>` arm at the end of deliver_job (~:1683-1697) carries the inline comment "Genuine failure (DB error or all provider sends failed). ... we log and move on rather than re-queue (avoids hot-looping on a permanently failing job)" and only emits `tracing::warn!(... "push delivery failed for queued job")`. Because the payload was already BLPOP-popped off the list before delivery is attempted, a TRANSIENT fault — an FCM/APNs 5xx or rate-limit, a momentary Postgres pool exhaustion while resolving device tokens, or a Redis/network blip mid-send — permanently loses that user's push notification for the remaining process lifetime. The queue's at-least-once intent (BLPOP drain of a durable Redis list) is silently downgraded to at-most-once for every transient blip. The code conflates PERMANENT failures (which correctly should not re-queue, to avoid the poison-message hot-loop the comment guards against) with TRANSIENT ones (which SHOULD get bounded retry/backoff or a dead-letter list). Mitigation that exists: the in-app channel remains the mandatory record, so this is a push-delivery DEGRADATION, not data loss — hence severity medium, not high. NET-NEW vs backlog: distinct FILE+MECHANISM from code-review-api-core-quiet-drain-drops-failed-delivery (that is quiet_hours_drain.rs's DB-held deliver_held drain, not the Redis BLPOP queue worker) and distinct from all prior push_fanout token/endpoint findings. Suggested landable (backend-only) fix: classify the NotificationError in deliver_job's Err arm into transient vs permanent (reuse the provider error taxonomy already present in the FCM/APNs adapters), and for transient failures either LPUSH the payload back with a bounded attempt counter + exponential backoff or move it to a `push_fanout_dlq` list for a later redrive, leaving only permanent failures to drop as today. Reachability traced statically (process_pending_jobs -> deliver_job -> adapter.send); runtime frequency of transient-vs-permanent not confirmed, hence confidence medium.
